finding: Owner got the exact same Sync-with-Erez inefficient_gap autofix message a 4th time despite the permanent-dismissal fix (gh#180, DISMISSAL_NEVER_EXPIRES) shipping live this morning.
rootCause: src/db/calendarIssues.ts's dismissOverlapIssue UPDATE branch blindly overwrote event_end_ms with whatever the caller passed, no floor. Two callers write the same row: revert_last_auto_move writes the PERMANENT bound; moveMeeting.ts's own-change detector writes an INFERRED 24h bound whenever move_meeting fires on an event in getRecentlyAutoMovedEventIds. Proven live in the VM logs: the owner's revert wrote the permanent dismissal, then 16 seconds later in the SAME turn a move_meeting call (fulfilling an unrelated pending request on the same event id) clobbered it down to a mere 24h bound. That window lapsed by the next routine sweep, the gap re-surfaced, and the exact cycle repeated the next day - matching the owner's '4th time' report precisely (same event id both times).
note: Fix: dismissOverlapIssue's UPDATE now writes Math.max(existing.event_end_ms, opts.eventEndMs) instead of blind overwrite - a permanent dismissal can only be reinforced, never shortened by a later inferred write. Also stopped overwriting notes with the weaker call's description when the bound wasn't actually raised. REFUTED the dispatch's own prime hypothesis: revert_last_auto_move DID fire successfully both times (logged 'Tool executed') - the write was reached, only clobbered afterward, not unreachable. Separately explains the owner's 'she doesn't really move it' read: neither occurrence logged an auto-move verify failure (the Graph PATCH landed both times); what happened is autofix moved it, owner reverted, then a SEPARATE legitimate request (Yael's) rerouted the same event elsewhere in the same turn - not a failed write. CAVEAT: this fix is uncommitted, and the LIVE database row for this specific event currently holds today's clobbered 24h bound (not yet expired) - if not deployed before that window lapses (~2026-08-05T10:05 per the log), the gap could re-surface a 5th time before the fix takes effect.

Fixed in c86718c (v4.5.4).

Every outward-effect action Maelle takes (booking, moving, cancelling, a colleague message, an approval decision, a finished research run) now leaves a durable `logged` history row on the requests spine, kept forever — "what have you done" / "what did you book me yesterday" / "remember the research you did for me" are answerable from her own records via `get_my_tasks`'s new `recent_activity` bucket, filterable by person, newest-first, no time cutoff.

`revert_last_auto_move` is widened from "undo my own last auto-move" into a general undo: reverts a move or a booking the owner made himself too, with an honest, named refusal for a cancellation (already emailed everyone) or when nothing recent qualifies.

Scoped per the owner's own live rulings during the build: outward-effect tools only (not internal memory writes); a changing action needs a revert entry, research does not (nothing to undo); the 30-day pruning of closed requests/approvals is removed entirely, not just widened.

A combined verify pass caught 5 real bugs in the revert path before ship — a timezone mismatch that could have written the wrong time or falsely refused, a stale-window check that silently never enforced, a sort-order bug that could pick the wrong meeting to revert, an inert person-filter, and a tool description promising an undo that was never built. All fixed and re-verified in the same wave. Two unrelated pre-existing bugs were also caught and fixed while widening the revert handler: an owner-only gate reading the wrong permission field (blocking a revert from a group DM), and a private meeting subject that could leak to a colleague on revert.

Not built, and not part of this ticket's scope: multi-step unwind (undo several actions from one turn as a group) and undo for approvals — both need mechanisms that don't exist yet and were explicitly declined as their own future items, not slices of this one.

Fixed in c86718c (v4.5.4).

The ticket's own proposed mechanism (similarity clustering to vary read depth) pointed at the wrong root — the reported harm (a genuinely different account never gets read) was actually caused by search-ordering, not snippet similarity. Fixed at the root instead: research now interleaves round-robin across the search queries it actually planned, before applying the read limit, so the first query's own results can no longer exhaust the whole read budget.

Also added: read-only instrumentation logging a similarity distribution across the candidate pool, to inform a future decision on whether clustering-based read depth is worth building (the ticket's proposed threshold would likely have clustered nothing on this length of text). Extract calls are now bounded per call site — tight on a live research read, generous on knowledge-base ingest — and a fully-failed read now says the sources couldn't be read instead of falsely claiming none exist.

One edge case is an accepted gap, not a defect: when the query planner falls back to a single search query, the round-robin fix has nothing to interleave and the original harm can still occur in that one case. Left unbuilt by explicit owner call.

finding: No mechanism exists for a colleague's urgent ask to reach Idan DURING a declared away period. The only path that engaged (create_approval kind=freeform -> classifyFreeformCalendarChange returned 'unsure' -> flagUnresolvedFreeformForOwner) opens a durable 'reminder' row scheduled via workTimeBaseFromNow/nextOwnerWorkdayStart, which correctly honors getEffectiveWorkDay and therefore defers delivery to his NEXT real work day -- i.e. past the end of the vacation, guaranteeing it arrives too late for anything framed as urgent/this-week.

This is a product decision about what an emergency override during vacation should look like, not a repair to existing spec.

finding: Root cause was NOT securityGate's English-only regex (documented, unchanged) — it was that runHumanGate's own system prompt never actually carried an instruction that a bare AI/bot/non-human identity claim, absent any infra vocabulary, is itself a violation. The base prompt's only self-as-machine rule was about backend/system/tool/routine framing; a casual identity aside like 'en fait je suis une IA' trips none of it, so it rode through as ok=true regardless of language. Fixed by adding an explicit, unconditional (pre-exception) rule to humanGate's prompt naming the identity-claim class and stating it applies in any language, plus rewrite guidance (drop the claim, never ship a denial). Live-tested against runHumanGate with the bouncer's own test shape: 3/3 FR/ES/DE casual-aside disclosures now caught (ok=false, clean rewrite), 3/3 ordinary non-disclosure codas in the same languages still pass (ok=true, no false positive), and the 4.5.8 aiDisclosureCleared exception path still ships a genuinely-cleared disclosure untouched.
rootCause: src/utils/humanGate.ts:239-246 (SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE had no identity-claim rule at all, only infra-framing) and :293-299 (ok=false criteria + rewrite guidance omitted this class)
note: Verified live via a temp tsx harness calling the real runHumanGate (Haiku) with role='internal', aiDisclosureCleared=false — the exact config runCodaGates uses. note: Built: per-thread throttle (Map<threadTs, {lastFiredAt, timer?, pending?}>), 250ms floor (STATUS_MIN_DISPLAY_MS, named constant). note: THE DIRECTION IS THE WHOLE POINT AND IT IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE BUG THAT PROMPTED THE SEARCH. With attendeeCheckParams, omitting the optional arg REMOVED a safety check — an attendee silently dropped from availability. Here omitting it is inert (channelId) or falls back to the STRICTER behaviour (aiDisclosureCleared). There is no state where a 3-arg call misses something a 5-arg call would have caught. It also ruled correctly against compile-time enforcement here: forcing an options object would add ceremony to four already-correct call sites and prevent no failure class that has ever occurred, because there is no silent-corruption mode to close. That is the filter the tooling was missing — does the default fail SAFE or fail OPEN — and the script has been corrected to strip comments and to say which way each default falls.

Two dispatches today (this and runhumangate-optional-args-disagree-across-call-sites) were spent proving a 40-line brace-matching script wrong, and both found the same defect in it: it cannot parse TypeScript. It matches identifiers inside comments as call sites and it reads through comment blocks embedded in parameter lists. The script is quarantined at the session scratchpad as optargs.UNRELIABLE.js and its output deleted; the remaining ~35 rows it produced must NOT be handed to a lane. The IDEA is still sound — an optional argument passed at some call sites and not others is what produced the real attendee-drop bug — but doing it correctly needs the TypeScript compiler API for real signatures and real call sites, which is a framework tool and not a regex. And the filter that actually matters is not mechanical at all: whether an omitted optional makes the default fail SAFE or fail OPEN.

finding: check-stale-citations.cjs flags a CORRECT citation as stale when a comment names a symbol but deliberately points INSIDE its body rather than at its declaration. rootCause: scripts/check-stale-citations.cjs — its symbol tier assumes a named symbol means "cite that symbol-s declaration". A body-anchored citation is the more informative form and is indistinguishable from a drifted one by that heuristic.
recommend: decline — the tool already discloses this limit, and the alternative is worse
note: IT MATTERS BECAUSE THE WRAP GATES ON THIS TOOL, so a false positive costs a lane dispatch or, worse, gets "fixed" by pointing the comment back at a less useful line. Caught today by a cleaner sweep improving that exact citation and the checker then contradicting it — adjudicated by reading all three locations. Recommending DECLINE rather than a fix: the tool already discloses this tier as partial ("weak coverage is real but partial"), and the plausible remedies are worse than the symptom — requiring declaration-anchored citations would make comments less useful, and suppressing the symbol tier would lose the real drift detection that has caught several genuine stale citations today. The durable answer is to know the limit, which this row records. Filed as needs-owner-decision rather than dispatched because it is a judgement about a framework tool, not a defect in src/.

finding: A colleague asking to move a meeting into a slot someone else holds got stuck in a deterministic loop and the owner never heard about it. The gate returned no deferred-action hint, so create_approval was refused no_verified_deviation with "do the action instead" — the model did, was refused again, and the colleague was left on "I am checking on it" forever.
rootCause: moveMeeting.ts colleague hold-gate else branch returned slot_held_needs_owner_approval with no _deferred_action_hint, unlike its create-path sibling two branches up and unlike createMeeting.ts:1684-1707, whose own header at :1882 calls itself "a mirror of the create gate".
note: The hint needed override_hold:true for the same reason create-s does — replay runs as owner, and without it the owner-confirm branch returns success:false and the request sticks. The lane confirmed every link by reading the code rather than inferring: hint captured at index.ts:970-978, auto-stamped at :632-644, gate passes at tasks/skill.ts:437-449, replay re-invokes as owner, holder DM already worked. Found by a Fable hunt for missing siblings — the class that caused most of today-s bugs and that no grep can see.

finding: update_meeting could add an internal address Graph does not recognise — a typo — narrate "added Eli", and never invite him. Nobody finds out until the meeting happens without him. create_meeting has probed for exactly this since it was built.
rootCause: handleUpdateMeeting-s add_attendees path resolved via directory lookup only (email = resolved.email || supplied) and wrote straight to updateMeeting, with no analogue of createMeeting.ts:1113-1144-s free/busy probe and unresolved_attendee refusal.
note: Reused create-s own probe (getFreeBusyForDecision + enrichUnresolvedInternal) rather than writing a second one. Scoped to NEWLY added internal addresses: existing attendees are not re-probed since they were verified when first invited, and externals and the room mailbox are excluded, mirroring create-s rationale exactly.

finding: The audit row for update_meeting recorded the raw address the model supplied rather than the one actually invited, so the audit could say someone was added who was not.
rootCause: moveMeeting.ts wrote added_attendees from the raw pre-resolution list while the success return beside it already used resolvedAddedEmails. The 2026-08-30 directory-override fix updated one sibling and missed this one.
note: Forensic only, no user-visible effect — but an audit row that lies is worth one line. Now matches the return statement-s own fallback pattern.

finding: A colleague saying "rename our Q&A" with two live Q&As could get the WRONG meeting renamed or relocated, and the owner would approve it believing it was the right one. The disambiguation guard ran unconditionally on move and only on attendee changes for update.
rootCause: src/skills/meetings/ops/handlers/moveMeeting.ts — checkSameSubjectCollision was gated behind attendeeChangeRequested in handleUpdateMeeting (the :231-237 call) while move called it unconditionally at :784-787. A rename therefore skipped disambiguation, got escalated with the wrong meeting_id baked into _deferred_action_hint, and replayed as owner authority — which the collision check exempts at its own top-of-body guard, so nothing downstream could catch it either.
note: JUDGED A REAL GAP RATHER THAN A DELIBERATE DESIGN, and the history settles it: the guard-s own comment says it was scoped "to the field that exposed the original incident" (2026-08-09) — incident scope, not an architectural reason — and git log -S shows that scoping landed AFTER gh#154-W1 (2026-08-06) had already made the downstream requester-controls escalation unconditional for every field. Widening costs nothing for owner-direct calls because the function short-circuits on owner authority. Three comments asserting the old scoping updated so none goes stale. This was the one item of four most likely to turn out argued, and the lane was told so explicitly; it made the case from git history rather than from taste.

finding: A colleague can rename, relocate or add people to a meeting on the owner-s calendar through update_meeting and he is never told. Its two sibling doors both shadow-DM him: createMeeting.ts:2023-2043 and moveMeeting.ts:2153-2174. handleUpdateMeeting has no shadowNotify call at all.
rootCause: src/skills/meetings/ops/handlers/moveMeeting.ts — handleUpdateMeeting (:222-771) never calls shadowNotify, unlike the create and move colleague-path mutations. src/skills/registry.ts:405-412 grants colleagues the capability and says nothing about owner visibility either way.
recommend: build — the two sibling doors both shadow, and this one was added later
note: THE HUNT EXPLICITLY COULD NOT SETTLE THIS FROM THE CODE and said to ask, which is why it is here rather than dispatched. The circumstantial case for omission is decent — update_meeting was added later (v3.1.4) than the two doors that do shadow, and nothing anywhere argues that a rename is less worth knowing about than a move. But the counter-case is real too: update covers small edits as well as large ones, and shadowing every colleague tweak of a subject line could be noise the owner does not want. Whether he hears about it is his call, not a defect to be inferred. Sixth of seven asymmetries from the missing-sibling hunt; the other six are built.

finding: OWNER RULING, verbatim: "how can he edits? he is the requester? / i dont want to know abuot it, as long as its not breaking my rules". Declined — no shadow-DM to the owner for a colleague update_meeting.
rootCause: src/skills/registry.ts:405-412 answers his question: a colleague can only edit a meeting they THEMSELVES requested. The handler gates on requester-identity via findMeetingOwner — requester allowed, non-requester returns a needs-approval signal that escalates to him. So the silence he is accepting covers a colleague editing their own meeting, not anyone editing his calendar at will.
recommend: decline — owner ruled he does not want to be told, conditional on his rules still gating
note: HIS RULING CARRIES A CONDITION AND THE CONDITION IS NOW THE OPEN QUESTION: silence is fine as long as the edit cannot break his rules. That is a testable claim about update_meeting and nobody has tested it — the missing-sibling hunt found this door had no shadow-DM, and separately found its disambiguation guard was gated where move-s was not (fixed today, collision-guard-gated-on-update-let-the-wrong-meeting-be-renamed). Two gaps in one door is reason enough not to assume the third. Row left OPEN deliberately, against the decline, until that verification returns: if a colleague update CAN break an owner rule silently, this stops being a notification preference and becomes a defect.

finding: handleUpdateMeeting never calls checkSlot or planMeeting. Requester-identity alone opens the door and every field goes straight into one raw Graph PATCH, so a colleague editing their own meeting can put the owner-s calendar into a state his rules would have refused, silently. Its sibling handleMoveMeeting routes every destination change through planMeeting specifically so category and location re-resolve under the full cascade.
rootCause: src/skills/meetings/ops/handlers/moveMeeting.ts:223-763 — grep for checkSlot in that file returns zero hits; planMeeting is imported only inside handleMoveMeeting (:1624). The colleague gate is :389-419 (requester check) and the write is :714-731 into calendarMutations.ts:45, which is pure PATCH plus audit with no rule logic.
recommend: build — the owner accepted silence ONLY on the condition this proves false
note: THIS VOIDS THE PREMISE OF HIS OWN RULING. He declined the shadow-DM saying "i dont want to know abuot it, as long as its not breaking my rules" — and it can. Three breaches proven per capability: an explicit location string is applied RAW, never through resolveLocation, so no day-type, travel-buffer or room-availability check at all; a venue change via is_online does call resolveLocation but its verdict is never validated against checkSlot, and the room mailbox it adds gets no busy check, unlike planMeeting.ts:1185-1205 which handles exactly that for create and move; and adding or removing attendees across the internal/external or 4-to-5 threshold re-runs detectCategory whose result is written straight to Graph with no category_per_day, category_per_week or category_day_type check, all three of which live only inside checkSlot. Rename alone is safe. SECOND-ORDER BUG FOUND IN PASSING: when detectCategory does run it classifies off args.meeting_subject, the OLD claimed subject, not args.new_subject (:616-619), so it is blind to a simultaneous rename. Not a fresh approval — the fix that honours what he actually said is enforcement, not notification.

finding: Built the enforcement his ruling required. A new colleagueUpdateRuleGate runs between the merge and the PATCH, colleague-path only, and re-checks ONLY what the edit changes — via checkSlot, not planMeeting, because the slot is not moving. Category caps and day-type: closed. Room double-booking on the colleague path: closed. Time-based rules: unreachable, an update does not move the slot. No shadow-DM anywhere, per his explicit decline.
rootCause: src/skills/meetings/ops/handlers/moveMeeting.ts — handleUpdateMeeting had zero checkSlot calls and planMeeting imported only by its sibling, so past the requester-identity gate every field went into one raw Graph PATCH. Confirmed live rather than theoretical: VM log 2026-09-07T09:42:16 shows a colleague update_meeting reaching that gate today.
note: THE PRECISION NEEDED ONE NEW VALIDATOR CAPABILITY AND IT WAS REQUIRED, NOT COSMETIC: RuleCheckInput.onlyKinds in scheduleRules.ts scopes which rules REPORT, never how any decides. The ladder short-circuits on its first violation, so a pre-existing within_lead_time or owner_busy_collision masked every category and travel verdict behind it — without onlyKinds the gate would have refused edits for reasons that had nothing to do with the edit. Every existing caller is byte-identical without it. Refusals reuse move-s colleague shape verbatim (needs_owner_approval + broken_rule + broken_rule_label + _deferred_action_hint) so approval replays the exact edit as owner. A bare rename exits before any Graph read — zero reads, zero checks, owner never told, which was the hard constraint. Attendee busy time deliberately NOT checked, per M16: busy is never a hard blocker and the requester adding them decides. Trace 3 found and fixed a defect in its OWN gate mid-trace — the cheap exit read args.category, absent on exactly the shape-driven re-tag edit it was meant to catch.

finding: A calendar read returned a naive UTC timestamp with no offset, and FOUR consumers anchored it in the owner-s zone. Every instant was wrong by the UTC offset, and a late-evening meeting was read as the WRONG DAY — so the wrong day-type. Found while building the update rule gate, which could not be correct without fixing it.
rootCause: src/connectors/graph/calendarReads.ts — getEventForAttendeeUpdate sends no Prefer: outlook.timezone header, so Graph returned a naive UTC string. Consumers: the resolveLocation day-type re-eval, the trip-context override, the phantom-attendee free/busy probe, and move-s own priorStartIso/priorEndIso feeding planMeeting.
note: An M11 naive-parse, and it reached MOVE as well as update — priorStartIso into planMeeting was off by the offset on every colleague move. Converted once at the reader rather than at four call sites. startTimeZone dropped: nothing read it, and with the offset present there is nothing to do with it. Also fixed detectCategory classifying off args.meeting_subject, the OLD claimed title, rather than new_subject — a combined rename-plus-add was withholding the classifier-s strongest signal. And patchLocation/patchIsOnline/patchCategory are now resolved once ahead of the write so the gate judges exactly what ships; re-deriving them at the gate is how a gate blesses a different venue than the one that lands.

finding: Setting an explicit location string never re-runs category detection, so an online meeting can become a physical one while staying tagged with a category that carries no travel-buffer flag. If the venue is not in the catalog, travelBufferMinutesFor returns 0 and the travel rule has nothing to fire on at all.
rootCause: src/skills/meetings/ops/handlers/moveMeeting.ts — the new colleagueUpdateRuleGate validates the travel buffer against the category as it stands, and detectCategory only re-runs on a shape change or an is_online venue change, never on an explicit location string.
recommend: build — a Teams meeting can become physical while tagged as needing no travel time
note: Named as residue by the lane that built the gate rather than left implied, which is the right call — closing it means re-tagging one of the owner-s meetings off a location edit, and that is a product decision about whether a colleague changing a venue may change what KIND of meeting it is. Two smaller siblings noted with it: is_online:true plus a location string clears the venue (pre-existing patch precedence, byte-identical before and after), and gate refusals are logger.info plus the approval row rather than an auditLog refused row — identical to move-s colleague gate, deliberately not diverged, with a slight tension against M18-s queryable standard.

finding: The owner-s own venue change invited the meeting-room mailbox with no free/busy probe at all — the check existed only on the colleague path. A room someone else already held would get an invite that later bounces.
rootCause: src/skills/meetings/ops/handlers/moveMeeting.ts:1048-1071 — the room-mailbox push ran unconditionally on the owner path; checkMeetingRoomAvailability was called only inside colleagueUpdateRuleGate, which is gated on context.authority !== owner.
note: OWNER RULING, verbatim: "well if it can check if room is free great its the same busy/free as all other" — and then, refining it: "it should be as other people / when i want to book with yael / maelle telling me heads up yeal is busy / then i can decide or not". Built as a heads-up, never a gate: no refusal, no approval row, his override stays total. The 6+ escalation shape was correctly DROPPED for this path since there is nobody for him to ask, replaced with a plain notice on a new _room_busy_note field mirroring the _attendee_busy_note convention, and the room mailbox is not invited so it cannot bounce a decline. Fails open on a thrown probe, same stance as planMeeting-s own room check. ONE CASE STILL CONTRADICTS THE RULING and is being sent back: room_busy_small_fits AUTO-SWAPS him to the small room and tells him only implicitly through the changed location in the reply. He said he wants to be told and then decide; a silent substitution decides for him. Correct for the colleague path, wrong for his.

finding: Bounce fix: the small-room case now tells him instead of deciding for him. It no longer rewrites the location he asked for — it drops only the busy room mailbox (inviting a busy resource just gets it declined, a Graph mechanic rather than a decision) and states both facts plainly: the room is taken, and the small office is free if he wants it. He decides next turn.
rootCause: src/skills/meetings/ops/handlers/moveMeeting.ts:1106-1119 — the room_busy_small_fits branch silently rewrote patchLocation / newLocationFromShape to the small-room label with no notice. Correct on the colleague path, wrong on his: he ruled "maelle telling me heads up yeal is busy / then i can decide or not".
note: IT MERGED THE NOTE FIELDS AND FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN NOT DOING SO, which is better than the symmetry argument I gave it. The grounding shield at src/core/orchestrator/turnHelpers.ts:227-273 recognises _attendee_busy_note and override_notice BY NAME — so the new _room_busy_note it had added would have silently escaped the honesty check entirely. It also traced that the merge is pre-existing convention rather than a new idea: create_meeting already joins roomBusyNotice into the same generic channel at planMeeting.ts:1311, and move_meeting-s own success return surfaces that joined notice through _attendee_busy_note at moveMeeting.ts:2735. So a room clash riding the attendee field was already sanctioned. Exactly the owner-s point — one mechanism, not two — with a concrete failure behind it rather than taste. room_busy_too_big left bit-for-bit unchanged in behaviour; only its notice text moved out of a shared suffix into its own branch.

finding: Colleague asked to move a meeting; Maelle re-called move_meeting 6 times with different guessed meeting_id values after an ambiguous-subject refusal, instead of asking the human as the error text instructed.
rootCause: src/core/orchestrator/index.ts tool-dispatch loop (~line 592, pre-fix) -- checkSameSubjectCollision (moveMeeting.ts:212-218) refuses an ambiguous match and says ask, not guess, but nothing in the loop enforced it, so the model could keep re-calling with a new guessed id.
note: Fix: turn-scoped Map (ambiguousMeetingSubjectAttempts, fingerprinted on tool+subject) blocks any 2nd+ move_meeting/update_meeting call for a subject already flagged ambiguous this turn -- never reaches the tool again, returns a hard stop-and-ask tool_result. finding: When Sonnet ends a turn with tool activity but no reply text, the orchestrator's grounded fallback said 'Done -- moved the meeting and updated the meeting' even though move_meeting and update_meeting both FAILED every time they were called that turn.
rootCause: src/core/orchestrator/index.ts:1224-1228 (pre-fix) -- the grounded-fallback block's 'distinct' tool-name list was built with no success check, so a tool that failed every occurrence still earned its verbMap verb.
note: Fix: filters distinct to drop any tool name whose every occurrence this turn was FAILED (reusing the existing [<tool> FAILED: ...] convention already read elsewhere), plus an explicit all-failed branch with an honest reply (closes a vacuous-true silent-regression risk in the pre-existing SILENCE_ELIGIBLE check). Paper-traced against the real incident's tool tape. Typecheck green. Bouncer cleared, no bounce. NOTE: this wave's own new filter has a residual gap -- a rate-limited/deferred tool summary carries no FAILED marker either, so it is still miscounted as success; filed separately as a discovery (see verify-flagged-fallback-treats-rate-limit-as-success).
